verdict.rationale: Increase documents webhooks and a List Events API, and a customer story describes ingesting webhooks for each step of the ACH transfer lifecycle. Holds are documented to reduce the available balance, so the core event-driven ledger is evidenced, but not every element of the story is. missing for 10: explicit documentation that balance reads reflect pending/in-flight activity (beyond holds), a documented guarantee of webhooks for every transaction state change across all rails, and independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a developer, the ledger is real-time and event-driven — balance reads that reflect holds and pending activity, and webhooks for every transaction state change so my system mirrors the bank exactly

citations.quote: Increase can reach out to your application so that you can take action (such as sending an email alert about the transaction to your user) automatically.
you can also request Events from the Increase API using the List Events API
ingest webhooks for each step in the transfer life-cycle
As money moves through the system, track every update through real-time network events to keep your customers up to date.
Holds reduce the available balance without moving money, and can be released when they're no longer needed.
See the live status of every payment, including when it's submitted to the Federal Reserve, acknowledged, and even returned.
